papers.summary: The paper develops a systematic way to predict and control the truncation‑induced correlation length in LoopTNR applied to the c=1 critical line of the six‑vertex model, using the seed of dimerization and the sine‑Gordon mass–coupling relation. It demonstrates that by calibrating the seed and applying counterterms, the critical regime can be extended to many renormalization steps, revealing the marginal truncation error that persists.

papers.title: Coherent quantum-circuit simulation of Mueller dipole branching at small $x$: multiplicity fluctuations and DIS phenomenology
papers.abstract: Mueller dipole branching at small $x$ is a stochastic process in which splitting rates depend on transverse geometry. We construct a coherent quantum circuit for a regulated finite-state version of this process. Poisson-clock uniformization controls the number of updates, while orthogonal event-history registers retain the splitting paths, including those leading to the same final configuration. The circuit prepares transition amplitudes from local splitting rates rather than loading a precomputed evolved distribution. Its statevector multiplicity probabilities reproduce the truncated-clock Markov result to numerical precision and agree with the full continuous-time Markov-chain benchmark within approximately $7\times10^{-4}$. To examine fluctuations beyond the small circuit, we independently simulate the Mueller cascade with continuous transverse coordinates. At the largest rapidity studied, its normalized fourth factorial moment is $1.81$, compared with $2.84$ for an equal-mean Yule process. We also determine multiplicity entropies and correlations between dipole-size sectors. Applying a fixed negative-binomial dipole-to-charged-particle response reproduces the rising trend of the H1 charged-particle multiplicity entropy toward smaller $x$, but does not fully describe the measured multiplicity distributions. These results demonstrate an explicit coherent encoding of finite-state dipole branching and clarify its relation to continuous-cascade fluctuations and DIS phenomenology.
papers.summary: This work develops a finite‑state quantum circuit that simulates the stochastic Mueller dipole branching process at small Bjorken‑x, reproducing known Markov‑chain results and enabling the study of multiplicity fluctuations and entropies in deep‑inelastic scattering. The authors compare their discrete‑time simulation to a continuous‑time cascade, finding significant deviations in higher‑order moments and showing that a negative‑binomial response can partially capture the rise of charged‑particle multiplicity entropy observed by H1.

papers.title: Colored Jones polynomial of figure eight knot and non-perturbative topological recursion
papers.abstract: The asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial of the figure eight knot is proved to be connected with non-perturbative topological recursion on the underlying elliptic spectral curve, following the proposal of Borot and Eynard.
papers.summary: The paper establishes that the asymptotic expansion of the colored Jones polynomial for the figure‑eight knot can be described via non‑perturbative topological recursion on an elliptic spectral curve, extending the Borot–Eynard framework to a concrete knot invariant.

papers.title: Schwinger-Dyson recursion, Gr\"obner elimination and graph combinatorics
papers.abstract: Schwinger-Dyson equations are a cornerstone of quantum field theory (QFT). Derived using integration by parts, they capture relations between correlators of different orders, forming an open, infinite-dimensional system. In zero-dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions, which is just a physical interpretation for multivariate Gaussian integrals with polynomial insertions, conventional Gr\"obner elimination can be used to express all higher-order correlators (moments) in terms of a fixed basis set. One consequence is a closed finite-dimensional system of differential equations for the coupling dependence of these `master' correlators.   An important application of zero-dimensional QFTs is in counting discrete geometric structures (as in simplicial approaches to quantum gravity). For the problem of counting labelled regular graphs, applying this Schwinger-Dyson closure results in a computational breakthrough relative to the existing state-of-the-art: for 9- and 10-regular graphs on $n$ vertices, a finite-depth, finite-width recursive formulation is obtained, making it possible to compute the total graph counts in $O(n)$ arithmetic operations.
papers.summary: This work shows how Schwinger–Dyson equations for zero‑dimensional QFTs with polynomial actions can be solved by Gr"obner elimination, yielding a finite set of master correlators whose coupling dependence satisfies a closed differential system. The authors apply this to count labelled regular graphs, achieving an O(n) algorithm for 9‑ and 10‑regular graphs that outperforms previous methods.

papers.title: Lorentz charges for Lovelock gravity
papers.authors: Ayan Chatterjee, Sahil Devdutt, Amit Ghosh, Avirup Ghosh
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct the charges associated with the residual local Lorentz transformations on a black hole horizon in the Lovelock class of theories of gravity. The horizons is assumed to be non- expanding horizons, \emph{i.e} a null hypersurface for which the expansion corresponding to the null generator vanish. Naturally, these hypersurfaces preserve only a subgroup of the full Lorentz group of the bulk, and the residual symmetries correspond to the little group which stabilizes the horizon null generator. We show that on the horizon, the Hamiltonian charge corresponding to the residual local Lorentz boost is the Wald entropy.
papers.summary: This paper constructs Hamiltonian charges for residual local Lorentz transformations on non‑expanding black hole horizons in Lovelock gravity, showing that the boost charge equals the Wald entropy. It extends the covariant phase space analysis to higher‑curvature theories, providing a new perspective on horizon microstate counting.

papers.title: Inverted Pendulum in the Sky: Floquet Stabilization of Cosmological Axions
papers.abstract: Many cosmological scenarios require a scalar field to sit near the top of its potential, which usually requires a fine-tuned initial condition. We ask whether the hilltop of an axion potential can be dynamically stabilized by a rapidly oscillating coupling, as for the inverted pendulum of Kapitza, and to what extent this can reduce the fine-tuning. Using Floquet theory, we determine the stability window of the hilltop and analyze several realizations: an oscillating coupling, a spinning or oscillating second field, and a gyroscopic analogue, an inverted spinning top realized by a sigma model on a squashed three-sphere. In an expanding Universe the stabilized phase lasts for a number of $e$-folds logarithmic in the hierarchy of scales, independently of the cosmological background. Classifying the stabilizers by how their effective frequency redshifts, we show that in these realizations the hilltop cannot both attract the field and leave it frozen by the Hubble friction during radiation or matter domination, and that during inflation the attraction is limited by the Hubble friction and the energy budget. Thus the simple realizations studied here do not generically remove the hilltop fine-tuning. They can instead delay the onset of the oscillation and enhance the relic abundance as $n_\phi/n_{\phi,{\rm std}}\propto(\tilde m/H_c)^{3/2}$ in radiation domination. We discuss the implications for axion dark matter, inflation, quintessence and curvatons.
papers.summary: The paper investigates whether a rapidly oscillating coupling can dynamically stabilize an axion field at the top of its potential, using Floquet theory to map the stability window and exploring various realizations such as oscillating couplings, spinning fields, and a squashed‑sphere sigma model. The authors find that while these mechanisms can delay the onset of axion oscillations and enhance relic abundance, they do not generically eliminate the fine‑tuning required for hilltop initial conditions in cosmology.

papers.title: Distribution of the ratio of the two smallest eigenphases of the Jacobi unitary ensemble
papers.abstract: We compute the joint distribution of the two smallest eigenvalues of the Jacobi unitary ensemble and the distribution of their ratio. We use a framework for calculating Janossy densities based on the Tracy-Widom system of ordinary differential equations. For the cases studied here, the leading finite-N correction to the ratio distribution, relative to its universal Bessel-kernel limit, is O(N^{-4}). This behaviour reflects a nontrivial cancellation of lower-order corrections present in the Jacobi kernel. Eigenphase ratios may thus reveal subtle finite-size effects in quantum-chaotic systems with particle-hole or chiral symmetry. As an exploratory arithmetic application, we compare the ratio distribution for the two lowest zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L-functions with the hard-edge limit for Sp(N). The data indicate that the N_{eff}^{-1} term vanishes, leaving an O(N_{eff}^{-2}) correction.
papers.summary: This paper derives the joint distribution of the two smallest eigenphases in the Jacobi unitary ensemble and shows that the ratio distribution converges to a universal Bessel‑kernel limit with an unusually small O(N^{-4}) finite‑size correction, revealing a subtle cancellation of lower‑order terms. The authors also compare this ratio distribution to the lowest zeros of quadratic Dirichlet L‑functions, finding evidence that the leading 1/N_eff term vanishes, leaving an O(N_eff^{-2}) correction.

papers.title: The Zero Mode Constraint in the Dirac-Bergmann Analysis of Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Type Equations
papers.abstract: We derive the Hamiltonian formulation of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (KP) equation from a singular Lagrangian by means of the Dirac-Bergmann algorithm. The Lagrangian contains an auxiliary field, which leads to an irregular secondary constraint. On the branch that reproduces the KP equation, all constraints are second class, and the Dirac brackets give the known Hamiltonian and Poisson operator. We confirm these results by the Faddeev-Jackiw method. Then, we consider fields periodic in the first spatial coordinate. In this case, the zero modes of the derivative operator lead to an additional secondary constraint on the mean of the potential. This constraint replaces the inverse derivative by its zero mean counterpart, and the resulting Hamiltonian is in accordance with the one of Reiman and Semenov-Tyan-Shanskii, up to normalization conventions. For decaying fields, the same condition is necessary for rapidly decreasing potentials to remain rapidly decreasing. We show that this constraint appears for a general class of KP-type equations. In addition, we classify the smooth solutions of the auxiliary-field action. We also relate our results to an existing quantization of the KP equation, for which the potential Lagrangian provides an action.
papers.summary: The paper develops a Hamiltonian formulation of the KP equation via Dirac‑Bergmann analysis, handling irregular constraints and zero modes for periodic/decaying fields and reproducing known Poisson structures. It also classifies solutions of the auxiliary‑field action and connects to existing quantization approaches.

papers.title: Spectral reciprocity for reductive groups
papers.abstract: For every finite subgroup $\Gamma\subset\operatorname{SU}(2)$, every connected compact or connected complex reductive group $G$, and every finite central subgroup $B\subset Z(G)$, we construct a degree-preserving linear Fourier isomorphism between the polynomial class modules of $(G,B)$ and $((G/B)^\vee,\widehat B)$. The transform exchanges central twists with characters of the actual grades and preserves the invariant polynomial contributions of the full centralizers. In degree zero it yields central-coefficient reciprocity under the Poincar\'e pairing on $S^3/\Gamma$.   In particular, $\Gamma$ admits equally many conjugacy classes of homomorphisms into $G$ and its Langlands dual, which verifies a conjecture of Kojima and Tachikawa.
papers.summary: This paper constructs a Fourier-type isomorphism between polynomial class modules of a reductive group and its Langlands dual, exchanging central twists with character grades. It confirms a conjecture that the number of homomorphisms from a finite subgroup of SU(2) into a group equals that into its dual, offering a new perspective on Langlands reciprocity.

papers.title: Measuring the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way
papers.abstract: The origin of the Milky Way's high-energy neutrinos is debated. Their flavor composition reflects how they are made and could help settle it, but remains to be measured. We show that IceCube and KM3NeT, which see the inner Galaxy in complementary ways from opposite hemispheres, could start resolving its flavor composition in about a decade. With upcoming telescopes, they would infer the $\nu_e$ fraction at the sources to within 27%. A first comparison of Galactic and extragalactic flavor compositions could reveal strong magnetic fields in extragalactic sources or neutrino decay.
papers.summary: This study proposes using IceCube and KM3NeT to measure the flavor composition of high-energy neutrinos from the Milky Way, aiming to constrain the neutrino production mechanisms and test for exotic effects such as magnetic fields or decay. It estimates that within a decade the experiments could determine the electron-neutrino fraction at the sources to about 27% and compare Galactic to extragalactic flavor ratios.

papers.title: KEBBABS: Kilometric Enhanced Balloon-Baseline for Axion Birefringence Search
papers.abstract: We propose a broadband search for ultralight axion dark matter through the rotation of laser polarization induced by the axion--photon coupling. Two stratospheric balloons flying at altitudes of 30--40 km form a free-space optical link. One balloon sends a linearly polarized beam to the other, which reflects it back to a polarimeter on the first balloon. The long physical baseline provides an alternative to the repeated reflections used in resonant optical cavities. We target axion masses in the range $4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{eV}\lesssim m_a\lesssim10^{-11}\,\mathrm{eV}$. The lower edge corresponds to a frequency of about $1\,\mathrm{Hz}$, below which gondola roll about the line of sight can mimic a polarization signal. At $m_a=10^{-14}\,\mathrm{eV}$, a low-cost Pathfinder using flight-demonstrated technology could probe couplings as small as $g_{a\gamma}\simeq2.8\times10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, about a factor of two below the CAST bound. At the same mass, the Feasible today configuration could probe couplings just below the astrophysical bounds considered here, while the Futuristic configuration could reach $g_{a\gamma}\simeq6.4\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, roughly two orders of magnitude below those bounds.
papers.summary: This paper proposes a balloon-borne optical link to detect ultralight axion dark matter via polarization rotation, targeting masses 4×10⁻¹⁵–10⁻¹¹ eV and couplings down to 10⁻¹⁵ GeV⁻¹ in a futuristic setup.
